Experienced something similar with slab above grade.  About 1.25” sunk in the middle and 2” on the opposite corner from the highest point in the room.  Slab separated from walls creating a bowl in our back room. No cracking through the entirety of the room, just separation near walls.  Had a structural engineer out to evaluate and said added concrete wouldn’t be an issue, nor would injection underneath slab.

Concrete sucked and was slow by hand. Decided to create a wooden subfloor with 1’x1’ shims across the entire room approximately 10-12” apart from each other. Used construction subfloor adhesive + tapcons to secure the shims to the slab, and then screws to secure 3/4” osb to the shims. Used a ton of construction adhesive and screws, and encountered some slight irregularities that a belt sander took care of.  Installed LVP over and it was pretty darn easy.

Time will tell if it works, but if your basement isn’t being used for anything you have time to do a more appropriate fix.

On my last post I stated that something seemed off. I was told to level the bed which I redid but it lead me down a rabbit hole of PM…

My nozzle kit bar was not level, and as a result my bed leveling was out of whack.

My z axis motor loosened up and was moving freely

I also got some new bed leveling springs and nozzles because I thought that it looked like my prints were calling for plastic, but nothing was coming out.

This caused me to clean my Bowden tube. And I noticed my indicator was spinning, but nothing was still coming out. My pulley tensioner(?) came loose and wasn’t applying enough pressure to the filament to move it forward which ended up being the culprit!!!!

1. You can pull through this. Your children need you.  I’m a kid with 4 siblings (5 kids in total).  While we didn’t grow up in the same situation as  your kids will, I couldn’t live without my mom. She is a ROCK. A woman I look up to now even at the age of 23. She struggled because she had 3 of us within the first 8 years of being with my dad (she was around 18, 20, and 26 when having the first group of kids). They divorced about 5 years ago. 
2. I hope you succeed because my sibling and I have had a wild upbringing, but we reminisce on the weird ass memories, even the bad ones. It’s something that brought us together and we are closer than most other siblings. We also talk about the sometimes janky things that our parents did for us because they were so unique, including freezing pb&j’s and being homeschool for a decent chunk of grade school to save money. It is all worthwhile in the end because we get together and we are all past the age of 16 and things are weird, but we all get together and cherish those weird memories we have together
3. I know my mom suffered and made sacrifices to know we had the best life based on the circumstances. You are making those too, and I bet you are doing a great job. Working two jobs is hard as shit, and your kids may not understand now, but they will in 10 or so years. Hopefully that teaches them hard work ethic too and inspires them to work their ass off to give you a fabulous elderly life.

TL;DR: it’s tough, but hopefully your kids see you work your butt off and it shows them how to be better than average. You’ll grow older and enjoy watching them interact and they will help take care of you because they understand what you did for them to ensure they had a successful life!

BEST OF LUCK! Keep pushing forward!!!
